about.title: Santa Cruz Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Cruz County recorded 159 injury collisions and 185 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with 1 traffic death — a stark reminder that even a single loss ripples through an entire family. Corridors like Rt 1, Ocean Street, Soquel Avenue, and Water Street see steady traffic, and crashes are more commonly reported on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters and evening traffic overlap. When a fatal crash happens on any of these roads, surviving family members are often left with grief, funeral arrangements, and financial uncertainty all at once. California law allows certain family members to pursue a wrongful death claim to recover specific losses tied to that death. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply help connect grieving families in Santa Cruz with an independent attorney who can walk through the legal standing rules, deadlines, and what a claim might involve, so you can focus on your family during an already painful time.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then certain dependents or heirs. An attorney can help clarify who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity can carry a much shorter window. Missing that window can end a family's options, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Clarity on What Can Be Recovered
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. A connected attorney can explain how these categories might apply to your family's circumstances.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to determine who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one in a Santa Cruz crash?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government entity or road, that deadline is often much shorter, so it's wise to seek guidance soon after a loss.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim depend on a criminal case tied to the crash?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may or may not be filed. Whether or not criminal proceedings happen, families may still pursue a civil claim for their losses.

items.question: Is there a pattern to when serious crashes happen in Santa Cruz?
items.answer: Public crash records show reported collisions in Santa Cruz tend to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., often along corridors like Rt 1, Ocean Street, Soquel Avenue, and Water Street. This is simply a pattern in the public record, not a judgment about any particular road.
